title: A Ledger for the Alibi
premise: When the coffin of town founder Eleanor Voss is exhumed for a cemetery relocation and found empty, retired detective Gideon Sterling is dragged back into investigative work she thought she'd buried with her old life. The case file from 1974 has been tampered with — by someone who knows it better than the current police — and every clue points toward the Voss family's living heirs, including Gideon's estranged first love, Miriam Voss. As the tide recedes to reveal what was hidden in the sea caves beneath the estate, Gideon discovers that Eleanor never died in 1974: she staged her own death to escape a murderous husband, lived decades under another identity, and her recent natural death triggered an inheritance clause that forces the truth into the open. The killer is the family lawyer who helped stage the original death and has been quietly embezzling the estate ever since; Gideon traps him by feeding him a falsified version of the recovered case file, and the final chapter closes with Miriam choosing love over duty as the sea gives up its last secret.
about_author: T. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing coastal town records before turning to fiction. They write mysteries where the past refuses to stay filed, drawing on a lifelong fascination with small towns that keep their secrets in salt air and silence.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Paper
chapters.summary: Gideon Sterling, running her failing bookshop on the edge of insolvency, receives a court summons: as a former lead detective, she must witness the exhumation of Eleanor Voss. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: weary reluctance, the ache of a life half-abandoned, and a flicker of the old sharpness stirring.

chapters.title: What the Ground Did Not Keep
chapters.summary: At the cemetery, workers lift the coffin and find it empty except for a ledger wrapped in oilcloth. The crowd murmurs; the current sheriff, Deputy Hale, is out of his depth. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: cold shock giving way to professional hunger she thought was gone forever.

chapters.title: A Ledger Written in Two Hands
chapters.summary: Examining the ledger at the bookshop, Gideon recognizes two handwritings: Eleanor's and someone else's — entries that read like coded alibis. She realizes the 1974 case file she remembers has been altered. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: unease deepening into obsession; the past feels closer than the present.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Came Back
chapters.summary: Miriam Voss returns to town for the exhumation fallout, and she and Gideon meet for the first time in thirty years. Old tenderness and old wounds surface over coffee neither drinks. POV alternating Gideon/Miriam. Emotional beat: love against duty — both women aware of what stands between them.

chapters.title: Case File 1974-11
chapters.summary: Gideon pulls the archived case file and finds pages substituted, dates shifted, a witness statement missing entirely. Someone with access — and knowledge — rewrote history. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: rising dread; this isn't a grave robbery, it's a cover-up still in motion.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Perfect Memory
chapters.summary: Family lawyer Aldous Crane offers help, reciting case details with unsettling precision — details not in the public record. Gideon notes it; Crane notes her noting it. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension masked as courtesy; first suspicion crystallizes.

chapters.title: Salt and Silence
chapters.summary: Miriam shares family lore: her grandmother Eleanor feared her grandfather Marcus, who died the same year Eleanor 'drowned.' A locked room in the Voss house has stayed shut for fifty years. POV Miriam. Emotional beat: inherited fear, loyalty to a dead woman she barely knew.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Forgot on Purpose
chapters.summary: Gideon tracks down Ruth Okafor, the missing witness, now in a care home. Ruth admits she lied in 1974 — paid to say she saw nothing on the cliffs that night. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: breakthrough and guilt; Gideon's own old investigation may have been compromised.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over My Shoulder
chapters.summary: The bookshop is ransacked; the ledger is nearly taken but Gideon had hidden it inside a hollowed-out decoy novel. Footprints, a dropped cufflink monogrammed with a C. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: violation and resolve — the enemy knows exactly how she thinks.

chapters.title: The Tide's First Offer
chapters.summary: An extreme low tide exposes the mouth of a sea cave below the Voss estate. Inside: a rusted strongbox containing Eleanor's real diary, water-damaged but legible. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: awe and urgency — the sea is cooperating, but only briefly.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Hand
chapters.summary: The diary reveals Eleanor planned her own disappearance in 1974, aided by a young attorney — Crane's father — to escape Marcus, whom she believed had killed her sister. POV alternating Gideon/diary excerpts. Emotional beat: grief and admiration; the founder becomes fully human.

chapters.title: Duty Calls Her Name
chapters.summary: Hale, pressured by the town council, orders Gideon to hand over all evidence or face obstruction charges. She stalls, knowing Crane has allies on the council. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: the cost of duty versus truth; isolation tightening around her.

chapters.title: Two Alibis, One Night
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing the ledger with the diary, Gideon reconstructs the night of October 1974: two alibis were manufactured — one for Eleanor, one for whoever moved the body. The second handwriting belongs to someone still alive. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: the puzzle clicking together, exhilaration shadowed by danger.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Crane reads Eleanor's will aloud: if her death is proven other than as recorded, the entire estate passes to a named trust — which he administers. Miriam realizes the empty coffin was no accident of time. POV Miriam. Emotional beat: betrayal and clarity; the exhumation itself was the killer's plan.

chapters.title: What Marcus Knew
chapters.summary: In the sealed room at the Voss house, Gideon and Miriam find Marcus Voss's own journal: he discovered Eleanor alive years ago and blackmailed her until his quiet death in 1991. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: horror layered on horror; every family story was a mask.

chapters.title: A Trap Made of Truth
chapters.summary: Knowing Crane monitors her, Gideon plants a doctored copy of the reconstructed file claiming the original ledger implicates him by name — bait built from real facts. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: cold determination; the retired detective sets her last, best snare.

chapters.title: Night at the Bookshop
chapters.summary: Crane comes for the fake ledger himself, and Gideon — with Hale finally convinced and recording — draws him into confession: he killed Marcus, forged the file, and arranged the exhumation to control the inheritance. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: taut climax; words as weapons, the trap springing shut.

chapters.title: Confession in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Crane realizes the trap too late and turns violent; in the struggle among the shelves, Gideon's old injury flares, but Hale arrives and takes him down. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: fear, pain, and hard-won victory; the case file finally tells the truth.

chapters.title: The Tide Gives Up What It Took
chapters.summary: At the season's lowest tide, searchers find Marcus Voss's remains in the deeper cave — proof closing every charge. The town learns its founder lived fifty hidden years under another name. POV Hale. Emotional beat: communal reckoning; grief and strange pride tangled together.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Last Entry
chapters.summary: The restored diary's final page addresses her heirs directly, asking forgiveness and leaving the house to 'whoever loved me without needing my name.' Miriam reads it aloud in the emptied Voss parlor. POV Miriam. Emotional beat: mourning turned to peace; identity reclaimed posthumously.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty, Settled
chapters.summary: With the case closed, Gideon faces her choice: a consultancy offer in the city or the bookshop and the woman who came back. She signs nothing, locks the shop early, and walks to Miriam's door. POV Gideon. Emotional beat: quiet courage; choosing love without abandoning herself.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Gideon begins writing her own account of the case — the true one — while Miriam reopens the Voss house as a public archive of Eleanor's real life. The last line of the ledger is Eleanor's, copied in Gideon's hand: 'Let the record show I lived.' POV Gideon. Emotional beat: resolution and renewal; the past filed honestly at last.
